hints.content: The arrow points to all values less than $-3$.
And the point at $-3$ is filled in.
So, the inequality represents everything **less than or equal to $-3$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**



[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at negative 3 and continues left. A closed point is plotted at negative 3 where the line begins.

choices.clue:
The graph of $x < -3$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at negative 3 and continues left. An open point is plotted at negative 3 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/d04fd2da61222ce74b83bca0d7746ede894949f1)

The graph of $x > -3$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at negative 3 and continues right. An open point is plotted at negative 3 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/63819088bb1652f01adb0f0486171a729136247d)

The graph of $x \geq -3$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at negative 3 and continues right. A closed point is plotted at negative 3 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/538eac1e1005b0fc4609bb6b7255012c58052232)
